headline: Medicare strength lifts outlook despite GAAP loss
summary_short: Adjusted EPS was $0.58 and GAAP EPS a loss of $0.14, with a health benefits ratio of 92.7%, flat y/y. Centene raised its 2026 adjusted EPS floor by $0.40 to above $5.20.
summary_long: Premium and service revenues grew 0.5% to $45.1B: Medicare rose 20% and Medicaid 4%, while Commercial fell 21% on lower Marketplace membership. Total at-risk membership was 25.7M versus 28.0M. Cash used in operations was $3.7B on payment timing. Centene repurchased $558M of senior notes and cut debt by $1.1B since June 30. Full-year HBR guidance narrowed to 90.4%-91.1% and revenue guidance is $196.5B-$200.5B.
confidence_notes: Prior-year adjusted and GAAP EPS were not stated in the portion of the release read, so no EPS delta is shown. Adjusted EPS is a non-GAAP measure reconciled in the release.

drivers.explanation: A lower Marketplace ratio from improved pricing and risk transfer and strong Medicare Advantage and PDP performance offset a prior-year benefit from a premium deficiency reserve decrease.
PDP premium yield and membership growth, Marketplace and Medicaid rate increases, risk adjustment transfers and state directed payments, partly offset by lower Marketplace and Medicaid membership.
Primarily driven by the timing of pass-through, premium and other payments, as expected.
CEO says solid fundamentals in core businesses produced a faster recovery in earnings trajectory than previously anticipated.
